bugs: Search does not escape LIKE wildcards, so `?q=%` matches every product (app/Models/Product.php:64). Minor.
antipatterns: resources/views/admin/products/form.blade.php:1 uses @props in a plain @include partial. The shared form should be an anonymous component (<x-product-form>), not an include that pretends to be one.
resources/views/products/index.blade.php:18 calls \App\Enums\ProductSort::cases() inline in the view instead of the controller passing the options.
strengths: Very thin controllers. Public filtering is a chain of named #[Scope] scopes (active/search/inCategory/sortedBy) fed by a typed IndexProductRequest::sort() returning an enum.
Route model binding via {product:slug} plus abort_unless for inactive products. Eager loads category for the list and the related items, and Model::shouldBeStrict is on.
The price_cents column name makes the unit explicit. The FormRequest normalises slug and is_active in prepareForValidation, uses alpha_dash:ascii, and ignores the current product in the unique rule.
Reusable x-form.field wrapper with @error, used on both the public filter form and the admin form, so filter validation errors also show per field.
Checkbox old input is handled correctly with session()->hasOldInput(). to_route()->with('status') flash, and a reusable x-flash in the layout.
Uses the framework's bootstrap-4 pagination view with inline CSS, so no build is needed and no custom paginator view to maintain. withQueryString() keeps filters.
Thorough Pest tests: datasets for validation messages rendered next to fields, filter rejection, sorting and pagination link query strings; a guest/non-admin matrix; assertModelMissing.

bugs: The search uses whereRaw("name like ? escape '\\'"), which produces the SQL `escape '\'`. On MySQL/MariaDB (default sql_mode) the backslash escapes the closing quote, which is a syntax error, so search breaks on MySQL (app/Models/Product.php:68-69). It only passes on SQLite.

Layout default title is config('app.name') and it is then suffixed with app name again, giving 'Laravel – Laravel' on pages without a title (resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php:1,7). Cosmetic.
antipatterns: app/Models/Product.php:65-69 hand-rolls raw LIKE SQL where whereLike/orWhereLike exist.
app/Http/Controllers/ProductController.php:30-32 binds a string $slug and runs a manual query instead of route model binding ({product:slug}).

app/Http/Requests/Admin/ProductRequest.php:34-40: decimal-to-cents conversion with float math (round($x*100)) adds logic and naming confusion (a 'price' column holding cents while the form takes dollars).
resources/views/components/product-form.blade.php:17 does number_format presentation logic inside the props binding.
routes/web.php:8 keeps the base welcome page at / instead of the catalogue.
strengths: The shared form is a proper anonymous component <x-product-form>, which picks its action/@method from $product->exists. This is the most idiomatic shared-form approach of the three.
Hidden is_active=0 input plus @checked(old(...)) handles the unchecked checkbox correctly. @class adds a has-error state on fields.
Public filter errors are shown per field with @error. Named scopes are used, and sortedBy adds an id tiebreaker for stable pagination.
Strict mode is on. Related products are eager loaded with category. A custom pagination view is set via Paginator::defaultView and works without a build.
Tests use viewData/assertViewHas, cover wildcard escaping, the price conversion, filter rejection and pagination query strings.

bugs: Public filter validation errors are shown only as a single generic alert ($errors->first()), not next to the relevant filter (resources/views/products/index.blade.php:20-22). Minor, because the per-field requirement targets the admin form.
antipatterns: app/Models/Product.php:29-32 overrides getRouteKeyName() to slug while routes/web.php:16 also uses {product:slug}. This is redundant and silently switches the admin routes to slugs too.
app/Models/Product.php:44-47 puts presentation formatting (formattedPrice) on the model instead of a reusable x-price view component.
app/Models/Product.php:71-76 hand-rolls raw LIKE SQL with an escape clause instead of whereLike.
resources/views/admin/products/_form.blade.php is an @include partial relying on implicit parent variables rather than a component with @props.
No Model::shouldBeStrict / lazy-loading prevention in AppServiceProvider.
strengths: ProductSort::apply() combined with ->tap($request->sort()->apply(...)) is a neat use of first-class callables, and it adds a stable id tiebreaker.
The LIKE escape uses '!', which works on MySQL, Postgres and SQLite, and is tested with a 100% Cotton case.
Reusable x-form.field and x-form.select components (options from pluck('name','id')) with @error and old() built in. The hidden-input checkbox pattern works correctly on a failed edit.
Thin controllers and FormRequests with prepareForValidation slug and boolean normalisation. Custom pagination view registered via Paginator::defaultView. withQueryString().
The largest Pest suite (38 tests): a guest/non-admin dataset, validation-message datasets, an old-input round trip, slug collision on update, and related-product assertions via viewData.

v.rationale:
I ran `php artisan test` on all three: impl-1 passed 37/37, impl-2 32/32 and impl-3 38/38. I also ran throwaway probes on each (old input on a failed edit, checkbox state, LIKE wildcards, unicode slugs, changing a slug, page out of range, query count) and deleted them afterwards. None of the probes found a functional failure on SQLite. The ranking therefore comes down to portability bugs and idiom quality.

**1. impl-1 (8.7).** The cleanest design. Named scopes take typed enum input, routing uses `{product:slug}` model binding with an inactive-product 404, eager loading is complete, strict mode is on, and `price_cents` is named explicitly. One `x-form.field` component carries `@error` on both the public filter form and the admin form. It uses the framework's built-in pagination view with inline CSS, so there is no custom view to maintain. Its tests are the most targeted: they check that error messages render next to each field and that filters survive in the pagination links. Weak points:
- The shared form is an `@include` partial that uses `@props`, rather than a real component.
- The search doesn't escape `%` and `_`, so a search for `%` matches everything.

**2. impl-3 (7.8).** Correct and well tested, with the largest suite, a neat `ProductSort::apply` used through `tap`, and LIKE escaping that works on MySQL, Postgres and SQLite. Weak points:
- `getRouteKeyName` overlaps with `{product:slug}`, which silently moves the admin routes to slugs too.
- Price formatting lives on the model instead of a view component.
- The shared form is an `@include` partial relying on the parent's variables.
- Public filter errors appear as one generic alert rather than beside each filter.
- No strict mode, and the tests leave a few unused variables.

**3. impl-2 (7.4).** Its Blade work is arguably the most idiomatic: a real `<x-product-form>` component and `@class` error states. But it has a real portability bug. The raw search SQL becomes `escape '\'`, which is a syntax error on MySQL with its default settings; it only passes here because the tests run on SQLite. It also adds ceremony: a type-switching field component, converting dollar input to cents with floating-point maths, and a manual slug query instead of route model binding. It also leaves the base welcome page at `/`.
